q: Ammonium nitrate fertiliser is manufactured by:
o: Heating ammonia with carbon dioxide under pressure
Treating rock phosphate with nitric acid
Passing nitrogen through hot calcium carbide
x: NH₃ + HNO₃ → NH₄NO₃; the solution is concentrated and made into granules. Ammonia with CO₂ under pressure is the urea process, the usual mix-up.

q: Using ammonium sulphate, (NH₄)₂SO₄, as a fertiliser year after year tends to make the soil:
x: NH₄⁺ ions are weakly acidic and are also turned into nitric acid by soil bacteria, and the sulphate stays behind, so the soil becomes acidic and may need lime. The fertiliser adds no potassium or phosphate.

q: Triple superphosphate is made by treating rock phosphate, Ca₃(PO₄)₂, with phosphoric acid instead of sulphuric acid. Compared with ordinary superphosphate, it:
o: Contains no calcium sulphate, so it has a higher percentage of phosphorus
Contains insoluble Ca₃(PO₄)₂, so it acts more slowly
Contains nitrogen as well as phosphorus
Contains gypsum, which slows its action in the soil
x: Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + 4H₃PO₄ → 3Ca(H₂PO₄)₂: no CaSO₄ is formed, so the product is not diluted by gypsum and is richer in phosphorus. Ordinary superphosphate is a mixture of Ca(H₂PO₄)₂ with CaSO₄, which is why the gypsum options are tempting but wrong.

q: A plant makes 80 kg of ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃ (80 g mol⁻¹). All its nitric acid is made from ammonia (1 mol NH₃ gives 1 mol HNO₃), and the acid is then neutralised with ammonia. What total mass of ammonia (17 g mol⁻¹) is needed?
x: 80 kg is 1000 mol of NH₄NO₃. Each mole needs 1 mol NH₃ to make the HNO₃ and 1 mol NH₃ to neutralise it: 2000 mol × 17 g = 34 kg. Counting only the neutralising ammonia gives 17 kg.

q: Bagasse, used in Pakistan as a raw material for paper and board, is a waste product of the:
x: Bagasse is the fibrous residue left after the juice has been pressed out of sugarcane, so it is a cheap source of cellulose fibre. The other industries do not produce plant fibre waste.

q: In cement manufacture, the dry process uses less fuel than the wet process mainly because:
o: The clinker is formed at a much lower temperature
No limestone has to be decomposed
No water has to be evaporated from the raw mix in the kiln
Gypsum is added before the mix enters the kiln
x: In the wet process the raw materials are fed as a slurry, and a lot of heat goes into boiling off the water; the dry process feeds powder. Both processes still decompose limestone and reach the same clinkering temperature, so those options are wrong.

q: Newspaper made from mechanical (ground-wood) pulp turns yellow and brittle in sunlight. This is mainly because the pulp still contains:
x: Mechanical pulping grinds the wood without removing the lignin, and lignin is oxidised by light and air to yellow products. Cellulose fibres are the useful part of all paper; choosing them confuses the part that stays white with the impurity.

q: In the Solvay process for making soda ash, Na₂CO₃, the main raw materials are brine (NaCl) and limestone (CaCO₃). The main by-product is:
x: Overall 2NaCl + CaCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂. Ammonia is recovered and reused, so NH₄Cl is only an intermediate; NaHCO₃ is the intermediate that is heated to give Na₂CO₃, and CaO is used up in recovering the ammonia.

q: In an oil refinery, cracking is used mainly to:
o: Join small molecules into larger ones for lubricating oil
Break large alkane molecules from heavy fractions into smaller, more useful alkanes and alkenes
Separate crude oil into fractions by boiling point
x: Heavy fractions are in excess, so cracking breaks them into petrol-sized alkanes and alkenes such as ethene for petrochemicals. Separating by boiling point is fractional distillation, the usual mix-up.

o: A heavy nucleus absorbs a neutron and splits into two medium-sized nuclei, releasing energy and more neutrons
Two light nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus
A nucleus emits an α-particle and becomes a lighter element only
Uranium atoms burn in oxygen to release heat
x: U-235 captures a slow neutron and splits into two smaller nuclei plus two or three neutrons, which can carry on a chain reaction; the lost mass appears as energy. Joining light nuclei is fusion, the opposite process.

q: A coal sample contains 72% carbon by mass. Considering only the carbon, how much heat is released when 1.0 kg of this coal is burnt completely? (ΔHc of C = −394 kJ mol⁻¹)
x: Mass of C = 720 g = 720/12 = 60 mol; heat = 60 × 394 = 23 640 kJ ≈ 23.6 MJ. Ignoring the 72% and taking 1000 g of carbon gives 1000/12 × 394 ≈ 32.8 MJ.

q: Thermosetting plastics cannot be melted down and remoulded for recycling, unlike polythene. The reason is that thermosetting plastics:
o: Have only weak van der Waals forces between their chains
Have a three-dimensional network of covalent cross-links between chains
x: Heating cannot break the covalent cross-links without decomposing the material, so it chars instead of melting. Thermoplastics such as polythene have separate chains held by weak intermolecular forces that heat overcomes, so the weak-forces option describes the opposite type.
